A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RILKE and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A.1–A.9. The changed title, added subsections and renumbered tables do not prevent reliable matching.

before.justification: v2 reports original knowledge-editing experiments on LLaMA and Qwen, including benchmark scores, ablations, routing analyses and generated-output case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds sequential-ingestion experiments, a RankRAG routing comparison and routing-failure cases.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 retain the robust intervention objective, frozen backbone, similarity-gated router and shared-subspace clustering algorithm. The new sequential-ingestion experiment varies the training setup without introducing a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions use UnKE, EditEverything, ZsRE and MMLU. The additions vary ingestion procedures, sample scale and routing evaluation within this retained coverage, without introducing new domains or task requirements.

E2.justification: v3 adds RankRAG as an evaluated routing/retrieval comparator in Appendix A.7.3 and a failure case in A.7.4. Original comparison sets remain intact; AnyEdit and UnKE also participate in the new sequential-ingestion experiment.

E3.justification: New Section 6.2 evaluates sequential versus joint ingestion over 10 UnKE clusters, averaging 13 items, with evaluation after each cluster and resets between clusters. Appendix A.7.3 adds a 15,000-edit ZsRE routing evaluation using Top-1 and Top-4 precision. Existing experimental protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a controlled sequential-versus-batched analysis, extends routing scalability analysis with RankRAG, and examines two ambiguous-query routing failures. Existing loss, layer, radius, clustering and representation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 introduces no repeated-run or seed disclosures, confidence intervals, significance tests or new uncertainty reporting practices. Averaging the new experiment over 10 sampled clusters concerns evaluation sampling, not repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are retained. New Table 5 reports original/paraphrase BertS of 0.742/0.723 for Sequential RILKE versus 1.000/0.834 for Batched RILKE. Table 12 reports RILKE versus RankRAG precision of 0.51 versus 0.48 at Top-1 and 0.79 versus 0.83 at Top-4. New qualitative misrouting outcomes are also reported.

T1.justification: The geometric properties, intervention equations, robustness derivation, routing definitions and clustering algorithm are unchanged. The added experiments introduce no new mathematical assumptions, propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about precise, paraphrase-generalizable, lifelong and memory-efficient representation interventions. The shift to 'knowledge memory control' changes terminology rather than the substantive contribution.

C2.justification: v3 explains sequential-training degradation through the absence of joint optimization and attributes routing failures to salient tokens associated with other clusters. It adds an interpretation supporting deferred shared-adapter retraining, while removing v2's explicit limitation about extra-large, continually expanding knowledge bases.

D1.justification: Existing implementation sources, paraphrase-generation disclosure and hyperparameters remain unchanged; v2 Table 8 becomes v3 Table 9. The additions specify evaluation designs but provide no new implementation configuration or code/data-access information.

R1.justification: v3 adds RankRAG and citations concerning safety guardrails, predictive analysis and spreadsheet generation. It newly positions the router against retrieval with reranking, while retaining the existing editing-method taxonomy and principal novelty arguments.

P1.justification: v3 changes the title and author/correspondence text, revises introduction and results paragraphs, subdivides Section 6 and expands Appendix A.7. The overall narrative remains intact. Section 7 introduces a visibly unresolved citation marker.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 5 and 12, adjusts table spacing and captions, and changes float placement, including Tables 2 and 4 and Figure 6. Existing figures and case-study displays are retained, with the same overall two-column layout.

improvement.justification: The sequential-ingestion comparison, RankRAG evaluation and concrete routing failures add useful validation and transparency beyond v2. The gain is limited: the sequential experiment uses small clusters with resets, and the 15,000-edit test assesses routing only. Removing the earlier continual-growth scalability caveat weakens qualification without outweighing the added evidence.
